citation: Open Climate Fix (2024). PVNet workshop paper, Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning at ICLR. https://www.climatechange.ai/papers/iclr2024/46
description: PVNet is Open Climate Fix's neural model and training code for predicting renewable electricity generation. It combines encoded numerical weather predictions and satellite imagery with recent generation, solar coordinates and location embeddings. Outputs are predictions of future energy yield. Geographic and temporal coverage follow configured input locations, training periods and forecast horizons; the README demonstrates British generation and European weather sources. Python source is free under MIT with training and inference instructions. A limitation is that the documented public satellite files currently use a compressor unsupported by the model's tensorstore backend, so those example paths cannot be used directly. Versions of the separate data sampler must also match. PVNet supports generation scenarios for electricity-system operation simulations and relates to PyPSA (model-pypsa). The linked ICLR 2024 workshop paper describes experiments. No private generation data or cloud account was accessed.
inputs: Recent generation, solar coordinates and location
name: PVNet renewable-generation forecasting model
